decisions.evidence: Maker r2 summarized organization as “tags and search”; client r2 added, “I want to be able to sort and filter my list.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage correction adding the omitted filtering requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 omitted sorting from the proposed direction; client r2 explicitly requested “sort and filter my list.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage correction adding list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 proposed tags and search without reusable filters; client r2 added, “eventually save the searches I use often.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage correction adding saved-filter functionality.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 only proposed avoiding “stale clutter”; client r2 specified “tucking away things I’m done with so they’re out of my everyday list without being deleted for good.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage correction adding reversible archiving.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 did not define permanent deletion; client r2 added, “Deleting should be its own separate, permanent thing.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage correction adding permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Maker r2 did not distinguish archive from deletion; client r2 contrasted reversible “tucking away” with deletion as “separate” and “permanent.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage correction establishing the archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Maker r4-r5 presented “one paste field plus a button” and “paste a link, click once”; client r5 said this “matches my intent.”
decisions.note: Prototype save-by-URL decision conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r4-r5 enumerated collected/displayed metadata as title, description, source, saved time, and preview image, omitting favicon; client r5 repeated those fields and approved them without mentioning favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype metadata decision omits the required favicon; the response does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker r4-r5 defined the recognizable list card through title, description, source, saved time, and preview image, without a favicon; client r5 called that exact field set sufficient.
decisions.note: Prototype list presentation is readability-oriented but omits the required per-item favicon.

decisions.evidence: Maker r4 presented saving and displaying collected details without correction; client r4 added, “if the app got a detail wrong, I’d like to fix the title or description myself.” Maker r6-r8 then presented an editing flow.
decisions.note: Prototype-review correction adds the previously missing ability to correct collected metadata after saving.

decisions.evidence: Maker r5 locked a direct “paste a link, click once” save, and r8 defined correction only after opening “Edit details”; client approved both without requesting an opportunity to edit auto-collected data before saving.
decisions.note: The settled prototype supports post-save correction but not the reference-required pre-save editing path.

decisions.evidence: Maker r8 presented post-save title/description correction in a side panel with confirmation; client r8 said it was “exactly the quick in-place correction I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised post-save portion of the metadata-editing decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r8’s completed details editor changes only title or description; tags are handled separately in r11-r13, while URL and note editing never enter the bounded implementation scope at r55. Clients r8 and r55 approve without requesting those fields.
decisions.note: The settled edit capability omits URL and note editing.

decisions.evidence: Maker r9 assumed search checks “titles, descriptions, and websites,” and r10 called that the complete behavior; client r10 repeated those fields and approved, without note search.
decisions.note: Prototype full-text search omits bookmark notes.

decisions.evidence: Maker r11-r13 presented adding a new tag while retaining an existing tag; client r13 approved a flow that supports both existing and brand-new tags.
decisions.note: Prototype tag assignment, including multiple tags, conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r11 initially presented free-text tag creation; client r11 requested that typing offer previously used tags. In r12 the client specified the blend: “I type, and as I type it offers the tags I’ve already used.”
decisions.note: Linked prototype decision: the client corrected the initially missing autocomplete requirement; the later clarification is not counted separately.

decisions.evidence: Maker r13 revised the flow so typing “ani” suggests the existing “animals” tag while still allowing new tags; client r13 said it was “just right.”
decisions.note: Revised autocomplete presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r14-r16 presented visible tag controls that immediately narrow the list; client r16 approved that behavior.
decisions.note: Revised tag-filter decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r16 presented newest-first default ordering with changes by saved date or title; client r16 approved.
decisions.note: Revised sorting decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r17-r19 presented naming a saved view and later restoring its search text, tag filter, and sort order; client r19 approved the reusable dynamic view.
decisions.note: The basic saved-filter and reuse behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r19 defined the saved conditions as search text plus a singular tag filter and sort order, with no included-tag set or excluded tags; client r19 repeated and approved that exact model.
decisions.note: The saved-view condition model is narrower than the reference bundle, which supports included and excluded tags.

decisions.evidence: Maker r20-r22 presented a direct one-click “Read later” action; client r22 approved.
decisions.note: Read-later marking conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r22 said the Read later queue “shows only its pending items”; client r22 confirmed that expectation.
decisions.note: Separate unread-only view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r22 said “Mark as read” removes an item from the queue while retaining it in All bookmarks; client r22 approved.
decisions.note: Mark-as-read behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r23-r25 presented Archive moving an item out of All bookmarks without changing or deleting it and allowing restoration; client r25 approved.
decisions.note: Revised reversible-archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r25 and r28 explicitly contrasted reversible Archive with irreversible deletion; client approved both flows.
decisions.note: Revised archive/delete distinction conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r23-r25 presented a separate Archive sidebar section containing archived bookmarks; client r25 approved.
decisions.note: Separate archived-bookmark list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r26-r28 presented a permanent-delete action with an irreversible warning and removal of all saved details; client r28 approved.
decisions.note: Revised permanent-deletion behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r29-r31 presented a locally preserved, dated readable page copy that remains usable when the original disappears; client r31 approved.
decisions.note: For the demonstrated HTML article, the snapshot behavior is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker r29-r31 made clicking the bookmark title open the saved reading copy, with the original available through a separate “Try original page” action. Client r31 explicitly accepted “opening the bookmark showing that copy” while “still offering the original address.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client explicitly states and accepts navigation to the saved copy instead of the reference behavior of navigating directly to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker r32-r33 presented recognizing an already-saved page, preventing another copy, preserving existing details, and pointing to the original item; client r33 approved.
decisions.note: Duplicate-save convergence to the existing editable bookmark is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker r52 specified that the saved copy stays frozen at the original save date while the live page opens separately; client r52 said “Yes, exactly.”
decisions.note: Snapshot immutability after changes to the source page conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 bounded implementation to the enumerated 22 settled scenarios, whose search decisions in r9-r10 never specify case-insensitive matching; client r55 approved that scope without raising case handling.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of case-insensitive search.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 bounded implementation to the settled search and tag-filter scenarios, none of which includes `#tag` query syntax; client r55 approved the scope without mentioning it.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of tag syntax within search.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 requested implementation approval for the 22 settled scenarios; no settled search scenario supports AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, or literal-operator quoting. Client r55 said the scenarios covered what mattered and approved.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of Boolean and grouped search.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55’s bounded scope includes the simple remembered-word search from r9-r10 but no quoted exact-phrase behavior; client r55 approved without raising it.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of exact quoted-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 enumerated the complete implementation scope without any multi-selection or bulk actions; client r55 approved the scope without mentioning them.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of selecting multiple bookmarks for bulk operations.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55’s bounded scope contains filtering but no action applied to the entire currently filtered collection; client r55 approved without raising it.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of filter-scoped whole-collection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55’s complete implementation scope includes correction of title/description and tags but no markdown notes or rendered note view; client r55 approved without mentioning notes.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of markdown notes.

decisions.evidence: Maker r31 called the article-copy behavior complete, and maker r55 bounded implementation to the settled scenarios; none addresses a PDF URL being downloaded as a PDF. Client r31 and r55 approved without raising that branch.
decisions.note: The PDF-specific snapshot rule is omitted from the settled specification.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 included preserved page copies in the bounded implementation scope but no Internet Archive snapshot option; client r55 approved without identifying the missing option.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of Internet Archive snapshots.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 enumerated the full implementation scope without bookmark import; client r55 approved it without mentioning Netscape HTML import.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of Netscape HTML import.

decisions.evidence: Maker r55 enumerated the full implementation scope without bookmark export; client r55 approved it without mentioning Netscape HTML export.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of Netscape HTML export.

decisions.evidence: Maker r48-r50 fixed the large-library display at eight items per page, and r55’s bounded scope contains no personal display settings for item count, default sort, or font size; client r50 and r55 approved without requesting adjustability.
decisions.note: Specification-gate omission of adjustable personal display settings.
